newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTHERN AFRICA PLANS INTERNET INDICATORS DATABASE.
newsitem.headline: SOUTHERN AFRICA PLANS INTERNET INDICATORS DATABASE.

text.p: Central bank governors across Southern Africa are working to develop a monetary and financial statistical database which will shortly be published on the Internet.

South African Reserve Bank Deputy Governor Timothy Tahane said on Wednesday the project was one of several being pursued by the central banks of the 12-nation Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) to forge closer regional ties.

Another area of cooperation was in the development of payment, clearing and settlement systems, Tahane told a conference. Payment systems were being developed on a national level but on a compatible basis, so that they could eventually be integrated relatively easily.
South Africa plans to launch a new Real Gross Time Settlement System allowing for intra-day settlement among banks early next year.
"Other SADC central banks are moving in the same direction with their own systems," he said.

The aim of such moves, following the establishment of the committee of bank governors 18 months ago, was to prepare the ground for a regional common market by 2004. SADC leaders set themselves the date as a target last year.
Tahane said achieving this goal was now within reach, but he urged faster progress in bringing down regional trade barriers.
"Formation of an economic community by the expected date means that the reduction of tariffs among SADC members ought to be accelerated," he said.
Another hurdle to regional integration was the exchange controls which all members, with the exception of Zambia and Mauritius, still applied to a greater or lesser extent.
Tahane said the central bank governors had established a subcommittee on exchange controls to devise ways of minimising the impact of such capital restraints.
SADC groups Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
